summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's fundamental behavior, tone, or output format consistently, or to teach it a specialized domain vocabulary that prompting cannot reliably enforce. RAG is the better choice when you need to inject fresh or proprietary factual knowledge that changes frequently, while prompt engineering should be your first attempt for most tasks because it is cheapest and fastest to iterate. In practice, many production systems combine a lightly fine-tuned model for style and task-formatting with RAG for up-to-date facts.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output structure, tone, or style that prompt instructions fail to enforce reliably across thousands of calls.
Fine-tune for domain adaptation when the base model lacks specialized vocabulary or reasoning patterns (e.g. legal, medical, or proprietary code) that cannot be supplied via context.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the knowledge is factual, large, or frequently updated, since retrieval keeps answers current without retraining.
Fine-tune to reduce latency and cost at scale by baking behavior into a smaller model, eliminating long few-shot prompts and shrinking token usage.
